elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Termination for Convenience. The Issuer may terminate this Agreement and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement for convenience..." The Issuer is the customer-side principal opposite the Servicer (Vendor); there are no Order Forms in this servicing structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical alias miss (the customer here is styled "Issuer", not a listed alias); in substance an unconditional customer election to terminate without cause is present.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer" — exactly 30 days, in writing, with no additional conditions, approvals, or cure prerequisites.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case the Servicer will refund pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), is owed by the Servicer, and is triggered by the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1: "The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement." Resignation is barred except on a legal-inability determination supported by an Opinion of Counsel, which is not a convenience right; the only other Servicer-side exit is the for-cause removal in Section 7.2(c) on a continuing Servicer Termination Event. Already met without edit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (though more favourable to us). The fallback level is therefore incomplete; the preferred level is the operative target.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, exit charge, or contingent payment mechanic is imposed anywhere in the cited or inserted language, and the insertion adds none. A cap is unnecessary where no fee exists.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply in a manner adverse to us: Section 7.1 denies the Servicer any convenience resignation at all, which is strictly stronger than confining it to term end. No term-end resignation right was added.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no Servicer convenience termination right (Section 7.1 No Resignation), there is no notice period to lengthen; the redline does not create one.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single inserted clause supplies elements 1–3 (Issuer convenience termination, 30 days' prior written notice, express pro rata refund of prepaid fees) and element 4 is already met by retained Section 7.1's no-resignation bar plus the for-cause-only removal in Section 7.2(c).

The deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" = false result is an alias artefact, not a substantive gap: the customer-side party in this transaction is the "Issuer", which is not in the standard alias list. The rendered operative text plainly confers an unconditional Issuer election to terminate without cause.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for an absent right, no deletions, no paraphrase of surrounding text, and no extras — "in whole or in part" was correctly dropped as surplus (no Order Form or partial-termination structure), and no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages, or procedural boilerplate was added. Retained favourable language (Section 7.1, Section 7.2(c) for-cause removal, Sections 7.3/7.4 continuation and successor mechanics) is untouched.

Intent is preserved: the insertion creates no undefined term and no dangling cross-reference; Sections 7.3 and 7.4 already operate on termination "under this Agreement", so successor-servicer and continued-performance mechanics engage without consequential edits, and the Section 7.2(c) removal remedy is unaffected.

Drafting clean-up (not a defect in substance, but repair before sending): the inserted clause is rendered as an unnumbered heading "Termination for Convenience." while the rationale and comment describe it as Section 7.7 — give it an express section number so it sits in the Article VII sequence.

Recommended conforming edit for clarity, not required by the checklist: Section 8.3 states the Agreement "will terminate on the earlier to occur of (a)... and (b)...", an apparently exhaustive list; add "(c) the effective date of a termination under Section 7.7" so the natural-expiry formula and the new convenience exit read together rather than as competing statements of when the Agreement ends.

Fallback level is deliberately not targeted and is not complete (30 days sits outside the 60–90 day band). That is the correct choice: adopting the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end convenience exit on 90 days' notice that Section 7.1 currently forecloses entirely.
